title: Certification budget with the 85-factory corpus (error bound at 95% confidence)
protocol: cluster-Hoeffding UCB on the marginal error/false-accept rate: UCB = Rhat + sqrt(ln(1/delta')/(2K)) <= r; K = exchangeable clusters (factories); delta'=delta (single pre-registered threshold) or delta/grid (union over the LTT 46-point threshold grid). Rhat=0.
headline: With the 85-factory corpus (label all 85) the tightest certifiable marginal error at 95% confidence is r~0.20 (grid-union) / 0.13 (single threshold). A 95%-accuracy claim (error<=0.05) would need ~1365 factories (grid-union) or ~600 (single) at 95% confidence; a 90% claim needs ~342 / ~150. The corpus is ~16x too small for a 0.05 bound.
note: If the claim is window-level rather than factory-level the count is smaller (9757 windows) but anti-conservative under within-factory correlation; the factory is the honest exchangeable unit. To certify each factory at error 0.05 you would need ~1365 labels PER factory (grid-union).
